fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/_engine_support/resolver.py` is a pure re-export shim over the stdlib-only
leaf `rebar._ids`. Its own docstring records why: the resolution primitives moved DOWN
to `rebar._ids` so `rebar.reducer` could depend on them without reaching UP into
`_engine_support`, which was a layering inversion and an import cycle. The shim was kept
only so existing importers would not have to change, and it says so: "New code should
import from `rebar._ids` directly."

ADR 0111 forbids internal shims. This one is the largest remaining instance.

Measured on `origin/main` at `50d5a36539d` by an AST census that resolves relative
imports and separately walks `ast.Attribute` and string constants
(`.rebar/scratch/census_resolver.py`). A line-oriented grep is not sufficient here and
an import-only census is not either; both undercount, in different directions.

- The shim re-exports exactly 9 names, every one under the SAME name it has in
  `rebar._ids`: `_FULL_ID_RE`, `_JIRA_KEY_RE`, `_SHORT_ID_RE`,
  `_resolve_via_binding_store`, `_scan_alias`, `build_alias_index`,
  `build_resolver_scan_index`, `resolve_ticket_dir_name`, `resolve_ticket_id`. The module
  body is imports and `__all__`; it adds no behavior. Only 5 of the 9 are imported by
  anyone through the shim — `resolve_ticket_id` (42), `resolve_ticket_dir_name` (16),
  and one site each for `build_resolver_scan_index`, `_resolve_via_binding_store`, and
  `_scan_alias`. The other 4 have zero importers and are carried only by `__all__`.

**47 files consume the shim, in three distinct reference shapes that need three
different edits.** Conflating them is how an earlier draft of this plan got the scope
wrong.

- **42 import-statement importers** — 30 under `src/`, 11 under `tests/`, 1 under
  `scripts/`. Heaviest clusters: `src/rebar/_commands` (12), `src/rebar/llm` (7),
  `src/rebar/_engine_support` itself (6), `tests/interfaces/lifecycle` (4). These need a
  module-path rewrite only.
- **4 attribute-access files** reach the module as a dotted path at call time rather than
  importing from it, so no import rewrite touches them:
  `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py:54`, `tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py:52`,
  `tests/unit/test_completion_sidecar_lock_loss_ab54.py:82`, and
  `tests/unit/test_relocated_store_repo_root.py:240`, each calling
  `rebar._engine_support.resolver.resolve_ticket_id(...)`.
- **1 string-literal site**: `tests/unit/test_completion_sidecar_material_balding.py:228`
  passes `"rebar._engine_support.resolver.resolve_ticket_dir_name"` to
  `monkeypatch.setattr`. This one carries a trap. Its target,
  `src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:265`, does a FUNCTION-LOCAL
  `from rebar._engine_support.resolver import resolve_ticket_dir_name`, so the name is
  looked up on the imported module at call time. After the rewrite the patch must target
  `rebar._ids.resolve_ticket_dir_name`, or it will silently patch nothing.

These three sets are disjoint: no attribute-access or string-literal file is also an
importer, which is exactly why an import-only census reported them as untouched.

## Change

1. Rewrite the module path in the 42 importers: `rebar._engine_support.resolver` becomes
   `rebar._ids`. Imported names are unchanged. Where a file already imports from
   `rebar._ids`, merge the two statements rather than leaving a duplicate.
2. Rewrite the 4 attribute-access call sites to `rebar._ids.resolve_ticket_id(...)`,
   adjusting each file's `import rebar...` line so the new dotted path is bound.
3. Rewrite the monkeypatch string at
   `tests/unit/test_completion_sidecar_material_balding.py:228` to
   `"rebar._ids.resolve_ticket_dir_name"`, and confirm the test still fails when the
   patched stub is removed, so it is proven to still be patching something.
4. Delete `src/rebar/_engine_support/resolver.py`.
5. Extend the held-out shim oracle `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`,
   which already sets the convention: assert the shim module is gone AND that the
   canonical path still works, so the test cannot pass vacuously.
6. Add a `docs/release-notes.md` entry recording `rebar._engine_support.resolver` as
   retired in favour of `rebar._ids`.

## Testing

- A new case in `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py` asserting
  `importlib.import_module("rebar._engine_support.resolver")` raises
  `ModuleNotFoundError`, and that `rebar._ids.resolve_ticket_id` still resolves a known
  ticket id — the positive half that keeps the assertion non-vacuous.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_completion_sidecar_material_balding.py` specifically, because
  it is the one test whose patch target moves and the one most likely to pass for the
  wrong reason.
- The existing resolver suites are untouched and must stay green; they already exercise
  these functions through `rebar._ids`.
- `make verify` for the whole-tree effect, including the import-convention guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `git grep -F 'rebar._engine_support.resolver' -- src tests scripts` exits 1
      with no output. On `50d5a36539d` it lists 47 consumer files plus the shim itself.
- [ ] **AC2** `git grep -F '_engine_support import resolver' -- src tests scripts` exits 1
      with no output.
- [ ] **AC3** `test -e src/rebar/_engine_support/resolver.py` exits 1.
- [ ] **AC4** `python -c "import importlib; importlib.import_module('rebar._engine_support.resolver')"`
      exits non-zero with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- [ ] **AC5** `python -c "from rebar._ids import _FULL_ID_RE, _JIRA_KEY_RE, _SHORT_ID_RE, _resolve_via_binding_store, _scan_alias, build_alias_index, build_resolver_scan_index, resolve_ticket_dir_name, resolve_ticket_id"`
      exits 0, proving all 9 formerly re-exported names remain reachable at the canonical
      leaf.
- [ ] **AC6** `ruff check src tests scripts` exits 0 with no output, proving no import was
      left unused or duplicated by the rewrite.
- [ ] **AC7** `pytest tests/unit/test_completion_sidecar_material_balding.py -q` exits 0,
      AND deleting the `monkeypatch.setattr` line in a scratch copy makes it FAIL —
      demonstrating the rewritten patch target is still live rather than inert.
- [ ] **AC8** `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py` gains a case covering this
      shim, and `pytest tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py -q` exits 0.
- [ ] **AC9** `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists exactly the 47 consumer
      files, the deleted `src/rebar/_engine_support/resolver.py`,
      `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`, and `docs/release-notes.md` —
      50 paths, and no other.
- [ ] **AC10** `docs/release-notes.md` gains an entry naming
      `rebar._engine_support.resolver` as retired, and the file's only diff is additions.
- [ ] **AC11** `make verify` exits 0.

## Ordering

Independent of the `_processors` re-export story — different modules, no shared source
file. Either may land first.

## Out of scope

- The `reducer/_processors.py` re-exports, a different shape (names forwarded from two
  sibling modules, not a whole-module shim), tracked on `censurable-exotic-snake`.
- Any behavior change in `rebar._ids`. This moves import paths only; resolution
  semantics are untouched.
- `docs/` prose mentioning the old path in historical narrative. `docs/release-notes.md`
  is in scope for an addition only, per AC10.
